why.title: The idea
why.text: 33…Qd8!! leaves the knight on c5 hanging. Taking it leads to mate.

why.title: What Black gives up
why.text: The knight on c5 is attacked by the b4 pawn and the queen on d4, and 33…Qd8 doesn't save it. That's a knight on offer.

why.title: If White takes the knight
why.text: 34.Qxc5 is met by 34…Qh4#, and it's mate.

why.title: White's best try
why.text: White's best is to leave the knight alone and play 34.Qg1. Black answers 34…Rxg1+, taking the queen on g1 with check. Then 35…Nd3 attacks the rook on e1, and 36…Qf6 adds pressure on the f4 pawn. Black ends up a piece and a pawn ahead: Black is winning (−6.90).

why.title: Why not save the knight first?
why.text: Saving it with 33…Nd7, the best way to do that, is clearly weaker (+1.14 against −6.90). White answers 34.Rg1, taking the open g-file, aiming at the rook on g8. That would leave Black a little worse.

points: The queen forks the king and the pawn: both can't be saved at once.

why.title: The idea
why.text: 36…Nd3!! offers the knight on d3. Taking it leads to mate.

why.title: What Black gives up
why.text: 36…Nd3 puts the knight on d3 where it can be taken by the queen on e3. That's a knight on offer.

why.title: If White takes the knight
why.text: 37.Qxd3 is met by 37…Qg1#, and it's mate.

why.title: White's best try
why.text: White's best is to leave the knight alone and play 37.Be1. Black answers 37…Nxe1, taking the bishop on e1 and threatening …Nf3 and mate. Then 38…Nf3 threatens mate, and 39…Qxf4 takes the f4 pawn. Black ends up about a queen's worth of material ahead: Black is winning (−10.62).

why.title: Without the sacrifice
why.text: The best move without the sacrifice, 36…Qd1+, is clearly weaker (−5.69 against −10.62). White answers 37.Be1, threatening bxc5, winning a knight. Black would still be winning, but far less than after 36…Nd3.
